title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
technique: speculative decoding: draft with a small model, verify gamma tokens in parallel with the target model using speculative sampling (exact output distribution)

optimized_metrics.evidence: we can make exact decoding from the large models faster ... show a 2X-3X acceleration compared to the standard T5X implementation, with identical outputs
an algorithm to sample from autoregressive models faster without any changes to the outputs ... without changing the distribution
the total number of arithmetic operations might be higher ... assume that we have enough compute resources to support the increased concurrency

headline_claim.text: We demonstrate it on T5-XXL and show a 2X-3X acceleration compared to the standard T5X implementation, with identical outputs.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: The expected improvement factor in total walltime by Algorithm 1 is (1-alpha^(gamma+1))/((1-alpha)(gamma c+1)).
metric_definitions.notes: speedup ratio of decode wall time vs standard decoding at batch size 1
alpha = 1 - E(D_LK(p,q)); expected tokens per target run = (1-alpha^(gamma+1))/(1-alpha)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Let c, the cost coefficient, be the ratio between the time for a single run of Mq and the time for a single run of Mp.

tradeoff_acknowledged: increases total arithmetic operations (e.g. several times more ops) in exchange for fewer serial runs
models: T5-XXL target with T5-small/base/large approximations; GPT-like on lm1b; LaMDA 137B (alpha measurement)
workloads: WMT EnDe translation, CNN/DM summarization, lm1b
extractor_notes: Pure single-stream latency (decode speedup); no serving load, no throughput or percentiles. Speedup is wall-clock relative to standard T5X decoding.
